### Hillclimb

**You own the metric and experiment integrity. Delegate the attempts.** One change, one measurement, keep or reject. Use [Perf issue](perf-issue.md) for one measured defect.

Read the [sign-off contract](../references/sign-off.md) before preparation or implementation and [run accounting](../references/run-contract.md) for attempts and receipts.

1. Run **how** to ground the workload and architecture. Name realistic dimensions such as data size, state, history, and concurrency. Reproduce the complaint before choosing a metric. Fix a metric and direction, realistic target, noise tolerance, regression gate, attempt/time budget, and stop predicate. A minimum trial count is appropriate when an early lucky result would mislead, not an excuse to spend an arbitrary number of trials.
2. Design a sensitive harness and baseline from safe existing checks or disposable scratch diagnostics. Vet it with **benchmark-checklist**. Contrasting realistic workloads must separate as expected. Present a proposal covering the metric, harness/product instrumentation, allowed changes, checks, bounds, and delivery limits. Stop for approval unless matching authority or an explicit scoped grant covers it. Build any shipping harness only after this boundary. Freeze workload, command, versions, tuning, sampling, work/error counts, and baseline regression evidence.
3. Open the **show-me-your-work** decision trail using its caller-assigned path outside product source. It owns the log format. Read previous attempts before the next; never introduce another TSV schema. Record the frozen baseline artifact and receipt in run accounting.
4. Ground each hypothesis in a named mechanism. For performance, use [Perf issue's ordered mantras](perf-issue.md), not its one-off stop rule. Reserve the attempt and delegate a tight covered scope to `implementer` or `implementer-hard`, with actual authority and baseline pointers. Use a fresh worker per independent attempt. Parallel trials require disjoint outputs, identical frozen conditions, and serialized integration, not workers writing one branch.
5. Measure each attempt before and after, alternating sides where noise matters, and run the regression gate. Accept only an improvement beyond noise with correct work and green regressions. Reject inconclusive/wrong-surface evidence. Revert only the attempt's own unchanged delta; preserve unrelated dirty work, and stop if another writer changed it. Within permitted commit limits, keep accepted fixes in verified order. Record the attempt either way, including artifact evidence and why it was kept or rejected.
6. On a plateau, change hypothesis category, re-read the source, or combine evidence-supported ideas. A more radical change beyond the approved scope requires a revised proposal and, if needed, a new harness/baseline. Never relax the metric or predicate to claim success. Correctness and simplicity outrank the number.
7. Stop at the target, budget, a justified plateau, a named user stop, or a blocker. This is active-session work, not an unattended wake service. Preserve pending ideas through [Pause safely](pause-safely.md). Run **review-panel** on accepted changes and [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) only within delivery limits.

**Reply:** metric/target, baseline/final and uncertainty, trial count, kept/rejected attempts, accepted fixes, decision and measurement paths, stop reason, and the best untried idea.
